analysis.title: "Peak Frustration": Gross Exposure Finally Cracks Into The Most Consequential Earnings Week Of The Year
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell about 50bps last week while two-thirds of its members finished green. Goldman's Brian Garrett says the week was when gross exposure finally cracked: it was the largest weekly de-gross since July, after net exposure fell about a month ago and remains in the 0th percentile.

Goldman's Prime book saw US equities net sold for the third straight week and four of the last five. Single stocks had the largest de-gross since late July, and global net selling was driven entirely by long selling, ahead of a week in which 44% of S&P 500 members report EPS.

Cash desk flows: long-onlies and hedge funds were both better sellers, led by TMT. The desk cites about $20 billion of TMT selling over the last two weeks, approaching July's AI unwind. Hedge funds dumped the most tech stock on Friday since September 2024.

Hedge fund P&L: fundamental long/short -1.1% on the week, -3.8% month-to-date and +8.8% YTD, after peaking at +17.4% in June. Systematic long/short -2% on the week, its worst week since 2024, -1.1% MTD and +18.7% YTD.

Last Thursday's move in Goldman's hedge fund VIP basket versus the most-shorted names was roughly -3.4%, in the same tail as Covid in March 2020 and DeepSeek Monday. It was the VIPs' worst day since 2011 and came while two-thirds of the S&P rallied and the index fell.

The GS momentum factor basket (GSPRHIMO) has had 30 daily moves of +/-5% in 2026, more than any year in the dataset (2000, 2009 and 2020 included) with two months left. Comparison years: 23 in 2000 (average VIX 23), 16 in 2008-09 (average VIX 31), 21 in 2020 (average VIX 29). 2026 average VIX is 18.1.
Goldman's momentum pair is back near -43% from its peak, close to its August low. Morgan Stanley puts the tech momentum trade down 62% from its highs while the S&P sits 2.5% below its record.

Goldman's AI winners vs AI-at-risk pair is down 13% YTD. The S&P ex-AI (SPXXAI) has outperformed the S&P by 7.4% in three weeks, the widest three-week spread in data back to 2006. The desk says it is in a de-gross episode where short-term stops outweigh medium-term fundamentals.

Nasdaq dispersion is unwinding: NDX 3-month implied correlation rose to about 0.33 from the high 0.20s, and the ratio of average stock vol to index vol fell from about 2 to about 1.75, consistent with the dispersion trade being forced shut.
Apple is negatively correlated to the Nasdaq 100 on a 3-month realized basis for the first time in a series going back to the early 1980s.

Bond CTAs have been heavily short fixed income for months but the global fall in yields broke their trigger (5.02% on the US 10-year was key). They are short about $300bn total (about $145mm DV01). A flat tape over one week implies covering $12bn DV01 ($25bn in an up tape), and over one month $42bn DV01 ($165bn in an up tape). Goldman's model has them buying in almost any scenario except yields rising.

Yields are falling alongside the AI selloff: over 10 days TLT rose about 5% while Goldman's AI basket fell about 15%. TLT 30-day realized vol is about 12, above the S&P's roughly 10.5, so bonds are more volatile than stocks.

Vol compressed somewhat after the prior Friday's panic bid, when delta-adjusted VIX hit roughly one-year highs, but 'scar tissue remains'. The NDX 1-week straddle priced 3%, near one-year highs, and the SPX 1-week straddle priced 1.8%, around the 60th percentile. The VIX market is more nervous than the SPX market over the next month: VIX 1-month 25-delta call vol is at an extreme while SPX 1-month 25-delta put vol is mid-percentile.

Cash and derivative volumes dried up into the weekend, which Garrett says points to lower gross. Equity CTAs are long $48 billion of global stocks, almost all US, and are sitting on top of medium-term thresholds in SPX and NDX below which more selling unlocks. NDX has already breached its medium-term trigger. SPX is about 2% above its own and is leaning on its 100-day moving average.

Sunday's Brazilian runoff was called by Garrett one of the most asymmetric macro events in recent memory, with the vol surface implying -22% / +13% for the outcome. EWZ 1-month put/call skew is around 1.66, the highest in data back to 2006. The article adds that Lula won over Bolsonaro.
Excess variance in SPX and QQQ priced for the US midterms is, per Garrett, 'exactly zero'.

Garrett leans toward being in the 8th inning of a significant de-gross episode rather than the 2nd inning of an AI ecosystem repricing. He wants bond volatility to subside, midterms out of the way, proof of AI capex payback in earnings, and oil below 90. The Zero Hedge author (not Goldman) argues none of the conditions are met and leans toward the 2nd inning, with the index still needing to catch down.

sector_views.rationale: TMT was the main source of selling. The AI winners vs AI-at-risk pair is down 13% YTD, the Goldman AI basket fell about 15% in 10 days, and tech momentum is down 62% from highs per Morgan Stanley. Garrett still favors upside call spreads on the AI basket as a rebound trade.

earnings_insights: 44% of S&P 500 members report EPS in the coming week, described as one of the most consequential earnings weeks of the year. Garrett wants proof of AI capex payback in these earnings for the de-gross to end.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A global retrace lower in yields through this level created technical demand for bonds and put bond CTAs in a position to cover shorts.

macro_indicators.reading: above 90 (Garrett says oil below 90 would help)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower oil is listed as one of the conditions for the de-gross episode to end.

trade_ideas.description: Upside call spreads on Goldman's AI basket (GSTMTAIP), Nov 105/120%, costing 2.75%
trade_ideas.rationale: Garrett leans toward the de-gross being in its late stages and hopes for a rebound if bond volatility subsides, midterms pass and earnings show AI capex payback.
trade_ideas.risk: Bond volatility staying high, midterm uncertainty, oil staying high, and weak AI capex payback in earnings.

risk_factors: Further CTA selling if SPX and NDX break medium-term thresholds.

Disappointing AI capex payback in the coming earnings week, when 44% of the S&P reports.
Continued forced unwinding of the dispersion trade and thematic rotation fatigue, with factor moves at record frequency.

tension_points.bull_case: Garrett leans toward the 8th inning of a de-gross episode, with the index recovering if bond volatility subsides, midterms pass, AI capex payback shows in earnings and oil falls below 90. He recommends AI basket call spreads.
tension_points.bear_case: The Zero Hedge author argues the conditions are unmet (bond vol rising, midterms priced at zero, oil far from 90, capex proof due this week) and the index may still need to catch down in a 2nd-inning AI repricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Garrett's checklist: bond volatility not subsiding, midterms unresolved, no proof of AI capex payback in this week's earnings, and oil staying above 90.
